analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, a test-only file. They cover staging-reservation release paths (bridge deadline refusal, cancel, refusal under pressure, close, shared-entry ticket accounting, attach at capacity, per-instance reservation namespaces), whole-root maintenance (TTL, global budget, epoch preservation, ownership proof, symlinked-ancestor rejection, temp ownership and age), the per-donation gate, and the write-behind queue bounds. The only changed ranges are in the write-behind admission tests (about lines 3444-3545) and a new range near 3685-3727 that was not visible in the supplied units. The change refactors tests to use production queue bounds (SSDPrefixCachePolicy.writeQueueMaxJobs and a derived queued-byte cap), and it adds a test that a sixth job is refused when queued bytes exceed the cap.

No production code is modified in the supplied evidence, so no new attack surface, regression or weakened control is introduced. The tests reinforce T-041 mitigations: bounded host memory in the write-behind pipeline, exactly-once KV budget reservation, release of staging on abandon, and refusal to touch unowned or symlinked files. They also reinforce the 30-minute TTL and global disk budget cleanup.

Limits on this conclusion: the patch excerpt is truncated, and the production sources (SSDWriteBehind, SSDWholeRootMaintainer, SSDPrefixCachePolicy) were not supplied. I could not verify that the tests match the real behavior or that any related source changes exist in other batches. Integration should confirm that any non-test changes to the policy constants (writeQueueMaxJobs, writeQueueSlackBytes) do not loosen the T-041 at-rest or memory bounds.
